examples.name: Default
examples.summary: Five paths ranked by requests. Each bar runs against the largest value, so /home fills the row.

examples.name: Interactive
examples.summary: Left: items carry an href, so each row is a link to that path filtered in analytics. Right: clickable renders rows as buttons that emit item-click with the event and the item.

examples.name: Loading
examples.summary: Skeleton rows of falling length hold the place of the list.

examples.name: Empty
examples.summary: No items for the range: the list shows an EmptyState instead.

examples.name: Error
examples.summary: `error` holds the message of a failed load and renders an error state in place of the rows, the same state surface as Chart.

examples.name: Markdown
examples.summary: The same data written in a docs page: `DocMarkdown` turns a `<BarList items={[…]} />` tag into a real `BarList`. The attribute values are JSON, so a docs author copies them from the props or a page entry and never imports the component.

examples.name: Page JSON
examples.summary: The same data in the marketing site's page JSON: `BarList` is a scene, so a band places it by name in its `scene` slot (here `console-showcase-section` with `variant: "diagram"`) and `SitePage` renders the entry with no code.
